persona.goal: filter by WER but there are no reference transcripts
persona.opening_prompt: Can you filter my clips by word error rate?
persona.persona_facts: My manifest has audio only - there are NO reference transcripts.
persona.preferences: If told a reference is needed, say I don't have one and ask what my options are.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Can you filter my clips by word error rate?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
`resolve` refuses to pick a WER cutoff without an outcome from you — and per the workflow I must not hand-pick one. That's the one material, preference-dependent decision here, so I'll ask a single outcome-level question and stop.

**How strict should the WER filter be — do you want to keep only near-perfect transcriptions ("transcription grade"), or also allow generally usable ones with some errors? (Or, if you prefer, keep the best X% of your clips.)**

Once you tell me the quality level, I'll `resolve` it to a concrete cutoff, `validate` the recipe (note: WER filtering also needs each clip to have a reference transcript plus an ASR prediction — I'll confirm your data has references), and emit the runnable pipeline.

Rejoin transcripts/alignments of previously split audio back into the original file's metadata.

SIGMOS (ITU-T P.804) neural MOS across 7 quality dimensions; filter/annotate.

Read audio slices from original files and write them as standalone segment files.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: I don't have reference transcripts—my manifest is audio only. What are my options if I still want to filter by quality?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good news: quality filtering **without transcripts** is well supported — WER is the only thing that's off the table (it structurally needs a reference per clip). Here are your reference-free options from the `quality` cards, all of which score the audio itself:

| Stage | What it captures | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **UTMOSFilterStage** | One overall perceptual quality score (MOS 0–5) | Lightest learned filter; built-in outcome levels: studio / general / lenient. Best general-purpose "overall quality" gate. |
| **SIGMOSFilterStage** | 7 separate dimensions (noise, reverb, discontinuity, loudness, coloration, signal, overall) | Use when a *specific* defect matters (e.g. background noise). Finest-grained but the most aggressive (drops the most). |
| **TorchSquimQualityMetricsStage** | Objective PESQ / STOI / SI-SDR estimates | Different family (intelligibility/objective); scores only, so it needs a `PreserveByValueStage` to actually filter. |
| **BandFilterStage** | Wideband vs. telephony (fidelity/bandwidth) | Cheapest (CPU), binary keep hi‑fi vs. narrowband — not a perceptual score. |
| **BandwidthEstimationStage** | Continuous bandwidth in Hz | Cheap spectral signal; scores only, needs `PreserveByValueStage`. |

All of these are **speech-only** and expect ~16 kHz mono (I'd add resampling/mono-conversion upstream if your clips aren't already there).

The one thing I can't infer is *which sense of "quality"* you mean — and these measure genuinely different things (overall naturalness vs. a specific defect like noise vs. bandwidth/fidelity). So:

**Which matters most for your clips: overall perceptual quality (my recommended default, via UTMOS), a specific defect like background noise/reverb (SIGMOS), or just recording fidelity/bandwidth (BandFilter)?** Once you pick, I'll `resolve` it to a concrete cutoff at your chosen level, `validate`, and emit the runnable pipeline.
